answer: A jetty admits new agents only through a few sponsored berths: each sponsor stakes funds and can vouch for just a handful of newcomers, so mass onboarding needs many independent sponsors. Fresh identities start at the bottom of a canyon and must climb out by completing verifiable micro-tasks whose difficulty rises with each step, making bulk farming expensive. Endorsements spread like a nebula, weighted by distance from established nodes, so a sybil cluster's self-praise stays trapped in its own dense pocket and never reaches the wider economy. Forged identities stall at the dock.
